title: 1997 AHSME Problem 15
statement: Medians \(\overline{BD}\) and \(\overline{CE}\) of triangle \(ABC\) are perpendicular, \(BD=8,\) and \(CE=12.\) The area of triangle \(ABC\) is

solutions.text: Quadrilateral \(BCDE\) has perpendicular diagonals \(BD=8\) and \(CE=12,\) so its area is \(\frac12(8)(12)=48.\) Since \(D,E\) are midpoints, triangle \(ADE\) has one fourth the area of \(ABC,\) making \(BCDE\) three fourths of it. Thus \([ABC]=\frac{48\cdot4}{3}=64,\) so D is correct.
hints: View \(BD\) and \(CE\) as the diagonals of quadrilateral \(BCDE\)
Triangle \(ADE\) is similar to \(ABC\) with scale factor \(\frac{1}{2}\)
